sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Bi–Sn binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset BiSn-08Li.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → (Bi) + (Sn), lies at 415.8 K.
The Bi–Sn system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as simple eutectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of Z. Li, Z. Cao, S. Knott, A. Mikula, Y. Du, Z. Qiao, Calphad, 32, 152-63(2008). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
For Sn, the liquidus meets the axis at 505.1 K.
Eutectic equilibrium L → (Bi) + (Sn) is found at 415.8 K and 58.4 at.% (L).
Table 1 compares the calculated temperatures with experimental values from the literature [3–5]; in this synthetic document those values and references are fictitious.
The upper stability limit of (Bi) is 544.5 K.
The solubility of Sn in (Bi) reaches 3.8 at.% at 420.0 K.
At 650 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 121 J/mol, at 64.0 at.% Sn.
For the equiatomic liquid at 650 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −3.42 kJ/mol-atom.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
